subject: Re: Redwood pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightlearn.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the asks we promised to follow up on:

1) Volume & budget
- BrightLearn estimated steady-state token usage: ~25M–50M tokens/month with campaign spikes up to ~200M in month-long events.
- Procurement indicated a target monthly budget range of $12k–$20k (tbd on committed volume / term).
- Samir: you mentioned a target closer to an effective $/1M-tokens in the mid-teens — please confirm if $15/1M is still the right target.

2) Caching assumptions (from call)
- Your app has a small static system prompt (~60 tokens) + repeated instructional prefix (avg ~90 tokens) across many requests. We discussed a prefix + KV caching approach where common prefixes and early KV keys are reused across requests.
- Our initial engineering estimate for this workload: prefix cache hit rate ~40%–55% depending on user behavior; with stronger reuse patterns (templated prompts + personalization via short suffixes) you can see up to ~60% prefix hits.

3) Pricing impact (high-level examples)
- List price (decode) used for examples: $20 per 1M billed tokens.
- Example math: if raw traffic is 1,000,000 tokens and prefix cache hits avoid 45% of generation, billed tokens = 550,000. At $20/1M billed tokens, effective cost per raw 1M = $20 * 0.55 = $11.00.
- With higher cache hit (60%), billed = 400k => effective $/1M raw = $8.00.

4) Next steps we’ll take (from Redwood)
- Share an annotated pricing model with scenarios (attached: pricing_model_v3.xlsx).
- Engineering will queue a short audit of your sample traffic (you mentioned sending BrightLearn_usage_sample.csv) to produce a more precise hit-rate projection and an estimated effective $/1M for your workload.
- Commercial: discuss a committed-tier discount that targets effective $/1M in the mid-teens, subject to a 12-month commit.

Ask for you: please send the sample CSV you mentioned (timestamps + prompt templates + avg tokens per request is ideal). Also confirm whether procurement needs an MSA/PO template up front.

Thanks — I’ll ping Marcus once we have the sample and we’ll work up the scenarios.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volumes: the 25M–50M range is accurate for our steady state; spikes are highly seasonal (we run 2–3 campaign windows / year). For the sample I’ll strip PII and send ~2 weeks of representative traffic by EOD today (attached: BrightLearn_usage_sample.csv).
- Prompt structure: system prompt is ~60 tokens and is fully static. We have ~6 templated instruction prompts (~70–120 tokens) that are reused across cohorts; suffixes for user-specific content average ~40–80 tokens. So we expect decent prefix reuse — likely in the 50% range, but engineering can surface better numbers.
- Budget: Procurement is aiming for a committed pricing band that yields effective $/1M between $12–$16, depending on commit.

A couple of asks:
1) Can you provide two concrete examples in the workbook: (a) conservative hit-rate 40% and (b) optimistic 60%, showing billed tokens, monthly bill at list and with a proposed committed discount?
2) What SLA/uptime do you offer for Dedicated vs Hosted? Procurement may ask early.

If you can get that workbook updated, I’ll loop in procurement next week for a short readout.

—Samir

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Redwood pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up

Marissa / Samir — quick follow-up from our pricing model side. I ran two scenarios in pricing_model_v3.xlsx and summarized below:

Assumptions: list decode price = $20 / 1M billed tokens (public baseline), commit discount examples shown for 12-month term.

Scenario A — Conservative cache (40% prefix hit)
- Raw tokens/month: 50,000,000
- Billed tokens after cache: 50M * (1 - 0.40) = 30M billed
- Monthly at list: 30 * $20 = $600k (list)
- Proposed committed price: $16 / 1M billed tokens => monthly = 30 * $16 = $480k
- Effective $/1M raw tokens at committed price = $480k / 50 = $9.60 per raw 1M

Scenario B — Optimistic cache (60% prefix hit)
- Raw tokens/month: 50,000,000
- Billed tokens after cache: 20M billed
- Monthly at list: 20 * $20 = $400k
- Proposed committed price: $14 / 1M billed tokens => monthly = 20 * $14 = $280k
- Effective $/1M raw tokens at committed price = $280k / 50 = $5.60 per raw 1M

Notes:
- The effective $/1M raw depends strongly on how much of the token footprint is cacheable (prefix vs suffix). The workbook includes a per-token-line example showing where savings materialize.
- For commercial outreach, recommend targeting a committed billed-price band of $14–$16 / 1M billed tokens for a 12-month commit to hit BrightLearn's target effective $/1M in the mid-teens (depending on hit-rate).

Next steps I recommend
1) Marissa: run the BrightLearn sample through the quick audit (engineering) to get a modeled hit-rate distribution (prefix vs KV vs dynamic).
2) I’ll update the workbook with both conservative/optimistic sheets and a recommended commercial term (12-month commit + standard MRR-style true-up).
3) Schedule a 30-min commercial + engineering readout the week of July 6 — propose July 7 or July 8.

Samir: if that works, we’ll draft a short mutual action plan after the readout.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
